scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to make my 7-year-old brother go to sleep when he stayed up late watching a movie with my friend. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that my brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep to grow and function properly. So, in an ideal situation, I should make sure he goes to bed on time. But last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to handle things. She even said it was fine if I had my one friend over. I made sure my brother went to bed on time, and then my friend came over. We were goofing around, watching a movie, and being kind of loud. That's when my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, and I said no, go back to bed. But my friend said we should let him stay. Now, I know that if I tried to force him to go to bed, I would basically have to drag him upstairs, and he would throw a fit. That would be embarrassing and exhausting, especially since my friend was there. So, I let him sit on the couch with us. By the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, my brother was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed. It was like midnight. The next morning, he didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8. He was pretty cranky. My mom found out I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I told her that since he's 7, he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later, he won't feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also mentioned that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? I need to think about this carefully. First, I need to consider the importance of sleep for a 7-year-old. According to experts, children his age typically need about 10-12 hours of sleep per night. If he stayed up until midnight instead of his usual bedtime, that's a significant loss of sleep. Missing two hours of sleep might not seem like a big deal, but it can have noticeable effects on his behavior and mood the next day. On the other hand, I was in a situation where I had to balance my responsibilities as the older brother and the fun time with my friend. I didn't want to ruin the evening by forcing my brother to go to bed, especially since he was already awake and wanted to stay up. Plus, I was trying to avoid a tantrum and the embarrassment that comes with it. I also need to think about the long-term implications. If I always give in to his requests to stay up late, he might not learn the importance of getting enough sleep. It's important for him to understand that his actions have consequences, and staying up late can make him feel bad the next day. However, I also need to consider his age. At 7, he's still young and might not fully grasp the concept of consequences in the same way an older child would. It's my responsibility to guide him and help him understand why it's important to go to bed on time. Another thing to consider is the role of my friend. My friend was there, and he was getting my brother riled up. That might have contributed to my brother not wanting to go to bed. I need to think about how to handle situations where external influences are affecting my brother's behavior. In the end, I let my brother stay up late, and he ended up being cranky the next day. My mom got mad at me for not enforcing the bedtime. I told her that two hours of missed sleep wasn't a big deal, but she still wasn't happy. So, was it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? I think it's a bit of both. On one hand, I was trying to avoid a difficult situation and keep the peace. On the other hand, I wasn't fulfilling my responsibility to ensure he got enough sleep, which is important for his well-being. Maybe in the future, I can find a middle ground. I can try to enforce bedtime but also be understanding and patient when he doesn't want to go to bed. It's a balance between being firm and being kind. I also need to communicate better with my mom about these situations. She trusts me to handle things, but she also has her own expectations. Maybe we can discuss how to handle such situations in a way that works for both of us. Overall, I think it's important to prioritize my brother's well-being, even if it means dealing with some short-term inconvenience. But I also need to find ways to handle these situations that are fair and reasonable for everyone involved.
